# Barrios Skills (John Manuel Barrios)

license: `MIT (repo LICENSE, "Copyright (c) 2026 John Barrios"). The vendored third-party skills keep their own terms: the Anthropic document skills say "Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms", and the K-Dense skills carry per-library licence lines.` · 12 skills · last update: 2026-09-17

**Source:** <https://github.com/Barrios88/barrios-skills>

**Maintainers:** John Manuel Barrios (Barrios88 on GitHub)

**Compatibility:** `cursor` `claude-code` `codex` `mcp`

> Mostly an aggregator. The repo ships 71 SKILL.md files, but its `scripts/sync-skills.py` builds `skills/` by copying whatever is installed in the author's local Cursor, Claude Code and Codex skill folders and a Dropbox folder. The README gives no per-skill credits. A provenance audit (md5 plus difflib word-sequence ratio against the RISE copies and against upstream git histories, 2026-09-29) finds 10 first-party skills, 2 adapted skills and 59 vendored copies. Only the 12 first-party and adapted skills are catalogued here. The 59 vendored copies are not double-counted. They are frozen snapshots, each changed only by an added `curated-by: John Barrios` frontmatter line and banner: 35 from K-Dense-AI/claude-scientific-skills, taken from its January 2026 versions (0.985 to 1.000 against those commits; dask, polars, pymc, seaborn, statsmodels, scientific-writing, peer-review, literature-review and others); 12 from meleantonio/awesome-econ-ai-stuff, already in the `awesome-econ-ai-stuff` pack at 0.94 to 0.99 (stata-regression, latex-tables, latex-econ-model, beamer-presentation and others). These are the meleantonio texts and not JonasWeinert/EconAgentSkills' rewrites, and Barrios is not the origin of the `latex-econ-model` skill that EconAgentSkills links to without shipping; 4 Anthropic document skills (docx, pdf, pptx, xlsx), taken via K-Dense's `document-skills` copy; 4 OpenAI skills (`doc` and `notion-research-documentation` from openai/skills, and the Codex built-in "PowerPoint"/"Excel" skills as `slides` and `spreadsheets`); 2 from hanlulong (econ-write and econ-slides, credited in ATTRIBUTION.md, already in `econ-research-skills`); 2 from lyndonkl/claude (academic-letter-architect and career-document-architect, 0.93 and 0.92, uncredited). The two adapted skills are `wrds`, an uncredited derivative of Edwin Hu's edwinhu/workflows `wrds` skill (0.744 against its 2026-01-10 version, with two reference files byte-identical) extended with a WRDS-MCP section, and `paper-2-acfin-web`, an accounting and finance rewrite of K-Dense's `paper-2-web` (0.115). The pack's most substantial original work is not a skill. It is `mcp/wrds-mcp`, a Python MCP server (about 1,800 lines, packaged as `wrds-mcp` 0.1.0 with Barrios as author) that exposes WRDS through nine tools: list libraries, list tables, describe a table, sample rows, run read-only SQL (validated by pydantic), download to CSV/Parquet/JSON, and ready-made pulls for CRSP returns, Compustat fundamentals and the CCM-linked CRSP-Compustat merge. It reaches WRDS's PostgreSQL through an SSH tunnel to wrds-cloud (a paramiko or sshpass daemon with `tunnel_up.sh`, `tunnel_down.sh` and `tunnel_status.sh`), so Duo MFA is approved once per session, not once per query. It uses the user's own WRDS_USERNAME and WRDS_PASSWORD. SEC EDGAR (stefanoamorelli/sec-edgar-mcp, AGPL) and OpenEcon Data (hanlulong/openecon-data) are not vendored. They get install notes only, paired with the `sec-edgar` and `api-data-fetcher` skills. The first-party skills lean toward accounting and finance: WRDS, EDGAR, pyfixest firm-year panels, FinBERT text measures, and Cochrane-style de-AI editing. Two need the author's own setup to work as shipped: `econ-lit-search` queries a private Meilisearch index whose host is redacted to a placeholder, and `web-scrape` assumes Yale's `curl_yale` proxy tooling. Authorship of `web-scrape` is the least certain of the ten first-party verdicts.
